# Chaofan Tao (陶超凡)

> Chaofan Tao is an AI researcher at LegoX (https://intellegox.net/), an open-source effort on agentic data, training infrastructure, evaluation, and models for coding agents. He is also a researcher at Huawei Foundation Model Lab. His work covers LLM coding agents, agentic reinforcement learning, agentic data and environments, multimodal LLM reasoning, and efficient LLM training and inference. He received his PhD from The University of Hong Kong (advised by Prof. Ngai Wong and Prof. Ping Luo, MMLAB@HKU) and his bachelor's degree from the Yingcai Honors College, UESTC. His paper on generative language model quantization received the ACL 2022 Outstanding Paper Award.

Key facts:

- Name: Chaofan Tao (Chinese: 陶超凡)
- Primary affiliation: LegoX; also Huawei Foundation Model Lab
- Education: PhD, The University of Hong Kong; bachelor's degree, Yingcai Honors College, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
- Research areas: coding agents, software-engineering agents (SWE-bench), terminal agents, agentic RL, multimodal LLMs, quantization and pruning, KV cache compression, scaling laws
- Award: ACL 2022 Outstanding Paper Award
- Publications: 27 papers since 2022 at venues including ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS, ICSE, ACL, EMNLP, COLM, TMLR
- Contact: tcftrees@gmail.com (internship inquiries: put "[Interest]" in the subject)

## Research overviews

- [Agentic Intelligence](https://chaofantao.top/research/agentic-intelligence/): an agent's ability lives in the loop around the model (seeing, acting, learning, being checked). Covers multimodal reasoning (NAVERO, PhyX, MMSearch-Plus, SRPO, SFT vs. RL for VLMs, RoboCodeX) and coding agents built in the open at LegoX: verified experience (LegoFlow, SWE-Lego, Terminal-Lego), SFT with error masking and RL inside real harnesses (Lego-RL), and agentic review and evaluation (SWE-Review, SwingArena, REAgent). Thoughts on the future: very long-horizon (weeks-long) agents organized around milestones that re-check the goal, verify progress, record lessons with their conditions and save state; keep experience at levels (weights, skills, memory with conditions); extra agents help only when they add independent evidence; evaluation is becoming the main bottleneck; in AI-for-AI loops judgment is the weakest link; AI for Science needs executable environments, provenance and replication on unseen settings. All works are by Chaofan Tao and collaborators, with venues listed.
- [Efficient ML & AI Infrastructure](https://chaofantao.top/research/efficient-ml-ai-infrastructure/): efficiency as keeping the information that matters. Covers quantization of generative models (ACL 2022 Outstanding Paper), structured pruning, UPop, CrossGET, vocabulary scaling laws, KV cache compression (D2O, UNComp, Prefilling-dLLM), asynchronous test-time scaling (ATTS), distillation (Adaptive KL, PerSyn), fault-tolerant serving (AnchorTP) and agent RL infrastructure. Views: infrastructure for large-scale agentic data (SWE and collaborative-office "cowork" data) is the new bottleneck; efficiency should be measured per trajectory; AI-for-AI loops should spend compute on verification; weeks-long runs need layered memory and resumable state; AI for Science should use cheap screening before expensive experiments.

## Projects (LegoX)

- [LegoFlow](https://intellegox.net/blog/legoflow/): agent-orchestrated framework for building verified coding tasks and training trajectories, from repository discovery to evaluation. Code: https://github.com/LegoX/LegoFlow
- [Lego-RL](https://intellegox.net/blog/lego-rl/): reinforcement learning inside unmodified coding-agent harnesses (e.g. OpenHands, Claude Code, OpenCode), preserving generation-time tokens and MoE routing for faithful training. Code: https://github.com/LegoX/Lego-RL
- [Terminal-Lego](https://intellegox.net/blog/terminal-lego/): executable tasks and grounded interaction trajectories for terminal-agent training. Code: https://github.com/SWE-Lego/terminal-lego · Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/SWE-Lego/Terminal-Lego-15k
- [SWE-Lego](https://intellegox.net/blog/swe-lego/): supervised fine-tuning recipe for software issue resolution with verified data, error masking, and curriculum learning. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01426
- [SWE-Review](https://intellegox.net/blog/swe-review/): agentic code review that closes the generate-review-revise loop for issue resolution. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06065

## Selected publications

- [SWE-Lego: Pushing the Limits of Supervised Fine-tuning for Software Issue Resolving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01426) (arXiv 2026): A supervised fine-tuning recipe for software issue resolution, combining verified data, error masking, and curriculum learning.
- [Scaling Laws with Vocabulary: Larger Models Deserve Larger Vocabularies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13623) (NeurIPS 2024): Compute-optimal vocabulary scaling connects tokenizer design with model size and training budgets.
- [Compression of Generative Pre-trained Language Models via Quantization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.10705) (ACL 2022 Outstanding Paper Award): Quantization methods that compress generative language models while preserving generation quality.
